Cc: Lina Torres <lina.torres@tidalwave.ai>

Subject: APAC launch — initial ask for dedicated pool sizing

Hi Rohan / Laura,

We're ramping up for our APAC product launch (targeting Singapore, Seoul, and Manila zones) and need Redwood to propose a dedicated capacity profile for the first 90 days. High level: estimated steady-state QPS is ~120 QPS across gen & chat endpoints (model mix below) with peaks up to 450 QPS during marketing promos.

Attached is an internal traffic matrix (tidalwave_traffic_matrix_v1.xlsx) with per-region forecasts and percentiles. Can you do two things:
- Provide a recommended APAC pool SKU mix (GPU types, count) for an initial commit that covers steady-state + 30% burst buffer.
- Provide an optional burst entitlement plan (how much immediate burst you can guarantee and pricing delta).

Model families: mix of Llama2-13B fine-tuned dialogue, a 7B embedding model, and occasional 70B gen for special reports.

We care about: latency SLO 95th < 300ms for chat paths, failover to EU if a node goes down, and a canary path before wide cutover.

Can we get a preliminary sizing by EOD Wednesday (May 26)? Also include any compliance notes for Singapore data residency.

Thanks,
Jamie
Director, Product Ops
TidalWave Analytics

Attachment: tidalwave_traffic_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
From: rohan_mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: APAC launch — initial ask for dedicated pool sizing

Laura / Priyom / Karthik — looping you in. Jamie sent their matrix and a tight deadline. Quick read: multi-model mix with occasional heavy 70B spikes; traffic is spiky but predictable.

Proposal approach (quick bullets):
- Tiered commit: Base (steady-state), Surge (sustained +30%), Emergency burst (on-demand with higher pricing).
- Model mapping: 70B -> large-oc (A100x2 equivalents), 13B -> perf-optimized 80GB, 7B embeddings -> quantized 40GB.
- KV/prefix cache sizing must be considered for chat flows to keep 95th latency under 300ms.
- EU fallback: is acceptable but must be shown as failover only (not primary), call out extra latency.

Questions for Jamie I want us to confirm before we size:
1) Are all tokens counted uniformly for billing or do they want splits by model family?
2) Any regulatory hold on Singapore logs / retention?
3) Preferred canary cadence (1% traffic -> 10% over 48h?)

I can draft a 3-option matrix and a cost delta per option. Priyom / Karthik can you run a quick simulation (traffic percentiles -> required concurrent tokens and VRAM mapping) and drop estimates here by EOD Tuesday so I can assemble a reply to Jamie by Wednesday morning.

—Rohan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jamie, thanks for the matrix — that helped. We've sketched a three-tier recommendation attached (provision_sow_draft.pdf) with estimated GPU counts, recommended instance SKUs, and a short canary/runbook excerpt. High level: 

Tier A (conservative commit) — covers steady-state + 10% burst
- 4 x 80GB perf GPUs (13B family)
- 2 x 2xA100-style nodes for occasional 70B jobs (queued scheduling for large reports)
- 2 x 40GB quantized nodes for embeddings

Tier B (recommended) — covers steady-state + 30%
- 6 x 80GB perf GPUs
- 3 x 2xA100-style nodes for 70B (pre-warmed cache for targeted routes)
- 3 x 40GB quantized nodes

Tier C (aggressive) — covers steady-state + sustained marketing peaks
- 9 x 80GB perf GPUs
- 4 x 2xA100-style nodes for 70B
- 4 x 40GB quantized nodes

Burst entitlement: we can guarantee up to 1.8x on-call burst for 24h windows for customers on an accelerated commit, with a step-up rate. We'll provide a per-hour USD delta in the SOW.

Compliance note: for Singapore residency we can keep control-plane and logs in a Singapore region with KMS key access. We'll call out retention and audit support in the SOW.

I've attached a draft SOW and a short cost sketch. Can you confirm whether they expect AZ-level separation (we can provide multi-AZ within region but it's a cost uplift). If yes, we'll add a zone-by-zone breakdown.

Laura Bennett
Director, Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: provision_sow_draft.pdf (3 pages, draft estimates)

Laura / Rohan — this is exactly the kind of breakdown we needed, thank you. A few clarifications: 

- We confirm the model families and token accounting — we'd prefer line-item split by model family in billing.
- AZ separation: yes please, provide the zone-by-zone split and the incremental cost for multi-AZ redundancy.
- Canary: we want a canary flow that starts with 1% traffic -> 10% over 24 hours, not 48. Can you include rollback criteria and the monitoring dashboards we'll get?
- Cost: can you provide a 30-day estimate for Tier B and the delta to burst entitlement?

If you can include a suggested DocuSign SOW timeline (we'd like to sign before June 10) that would be great. Also include an estimated lead time for pre-warming 70B nodes (we assume 6–12 hours).

I'll loop EngOps (ops@tidalwave.ai) if they need to see the AZ spread.

Thanks,
Jamie
